In this regard, the approaches of summer substantially augment
posts.content_html:
Aggressive and invasive, European wasps are among the most rampant pests affecting Australia, especially Melbourne. It is what sets them apart from others in that their stings are painful and have the potential to set off allergic reactions to human beings. In this regard, the approaches of summer substantially augment the likelihood of encountering these wasps around homes and other outdoor settings. In the following guide, one will find the behavior of European wasps, the dangers they pose, and efficient ways of dealing with wasp infestations.

7 State Pest Control – which is based in Melbourne – specializes in removing wasps for a safe environment.

What Are European Wasps?

European wasps are from the Vespula germanica species and, although these insects are native to Europe, in Australia, they have become an invasive species. The majority of these insects tend to be mistaken for either the native bees or other different species because of their likeness in appearance; however, European wasps can be easily spotted from their yellow and black markings, slim body, and aggressive behavior than most species. Most importantly, bees die after delivering their sting, but European wasps can remove their stinger to give stings many times.

Behavior Understanding of European Wasp

It would be good to know about the behavior of European wasps before attempting to get rid of them. Their interest in high-protein food shows significant attraction during spring and summer for feeding their larvae. In the latter part of this season, though, they become most attracted to sugary foods such as fruits, soda, and sweets. European wasps are merciless and sting and do so to attack because they cannot be annoyed as in the case of bees.

European wasps are a pest species, loved for their desire to nest in the most secluded spots. Examples include roof space, garden shed, eaves, and inside cavity walls or underground. A nest founded by a queen wasp in early spring begins small but can grow quickly over the course of the season, ultimately housing thousands of worker wasps by the end of summer.

Why Are European Wasps a Problem?

European wasps are very territorial and hostile. They can nest on an urban property, your backyard, a roof cavity, wall cavity, or even underground. Over the warm season in Melbourne, these wasps become extremely dangerous while interfering with their nests, which leads to swarming and, subsequently, multiple stings. They can’t resist food and sweet beverages over the warm season, making outdoor dining a bit of a danger zone.

These are some of the major issues caused by European wasps:

  • Intense Pain: The stings from European wasps can be used over and over again and will cause a lot of discomfort, and sometimes it also triggers high allergic reactions.
  • Urban Nests: Wasps build enormous nests that can be used by up to a thousand wasps. These nests destroy property and make outside areas uninviting and hostile to families.
  • Aggressive Behavior: European wasps act aggressively when they are in search of food or when their nests are threatened.
How to Get Rid of European Wasps

Here is how to safely remove the European wasps from your property step by step.

  1. Find the Nest

The first step towards controlling a wasp infestation begins with locating the nest. European wasps construct their nests in sheltered, secluded areas. Conduct an examination around your home and property and observe signs of wasps coming into and out of particular areas, perhaps roof spaces, sheds, or underground burrows. Once identified, leave the nest alone since wasps can turn highly aggressive if their nest is disturbed.

  1. Remove Food and Attractants

European wasps are very avid feeders, especially on meats, sweet dishes and drinks. To discourage wasps from landing in your space, ensure to:

  • Cover your food and drinks while eating outside.
  • Dispose of garbage in the bins with tightly shut lids.
  • Clean food crumbs or spills.
  • Don’t let pet food lie outdoors for a long time.

Removing foodstuff sources removes most of the wasps in the area.

 

  1. Use Wasp Traps

Wasp traps utilize attractants such as liquid sugary substances to capture many European wasps. The trappings lure the wasps into a container from which they cannot exit. Even though traps would not eliminate an entire nest of European wasps, they do reduce the activity of the wasps in and around your property, thus making the outdoors safer to enter.

  1. DIY Nest Removal – Proceed with Caution

Removing small wasp nests is sometimes encouraged for DIY removal by the masses. However, this is highly dangerous especially with European wasps. If you are to attempt any removal yourself, then be safe by first taking the following pre-cautions:

  • Putting on protective clothing: wear thick, protective clothing, gloves, and a face mask to reduce the potential of getting stung.
  • Wasp Spray: Buy a wasp-targeted pesticide, wait for late evening or early morning when wasps are less active, and spray the nest.
  • Distance: Keep a safe distance from the nest and have an exit route in case the wasps get vicious.

While DIY methods are effective, they may be relatively hazardous. It is better to hire a professional if you have infested large nests or pestering infestations.

  1. Hire a professional pest control service

A perfect way to eliminate European wasps is through hiring a professional pest control service. 7 State Pest Control boasts the best in Melbourne wasp removal services, with highly skilled experts trained to take on any size of wasp infestation. We can identify and remove nests using safe yet effective methods while keeping your family and property completely out of harm’s way.

Our crew can review the situation, find any hidden nests, and administer professional-grade treatments that remove the issue at its roots. We will also provide you with information on how to prevent this issue from happening again, including identifying and sealing points of entry.

Preventative Measures: How to Repel European Wasps

As soon as you have found yourself dealing with an infestation of wasps, you then want to take measures to avoid them returning. The following is some advice on how to keep European wasps away from your premises:

  • Seal Entrances: Look for your house holes, gaps, or cracks in your walls, roofs, and windows where the wasps are infesting and nesting. Close these possible entrance points so they can’t again get in to infest.
  • Install Screens: Screen your doors and windows with screens such that wasps cannot intrude your house.
  • Limit Sweet Smells: Wasps love sweet smells. Such fragrances attract them, including perfumes, flowers, and sugary food items. Outdoors, try to limit using pungent fragrances that attract wasps.
  • Secure Rubbish Bins: Ensure your outdoor bins are sealed tightly and emptied frequently enough to minimize the chance of attracting wasps to your place.
  • Keep Your Garden Well Trimming: Maintain trees, bushes, and shrubs in your home in a way that reduces the number of places where wasps can nest.

These wasps are definitely a nuisance, especially in the warmer months of Melbourne. Whether it is a nest that is still actively used or just working out ways to prevent future infestations, these wasps must be taken care of right away. Where minor problems are sometimes solved with homemade remedies, hiring professional pest control to handle the situation is the best way to ensure your property and home are protected from the unwanted presence of this buzzing creature.

If you need wasp removal services in Melbourne, 7 State Pest Control is available to cater to your needs. Call now and book your scheduled consultation to ensure that your place is freed of these aggressive pests.

posts.content_html:
Rats are one of the common pests found in Australia, mostly in urban areas like Melbourne. These rodents are not only simply a nuisance but are also significant health risks due to diseases carried and damage your properties may suffer. If you heard scurrying sounds in your ceiling or saw signs of rats in the house, taking immediate action is a must so that infestation does not reach a full-blown state. In this blog, we will guide you on how to get rid of rats in the roof with insights coming from 7 State Pest Control, a leading provider of pest control in Melbourne for rats.

Why Rats Infest Roofs?

Rats are opportunistic, always on the lookout for food, water, and shelter. Roofs come out especially in homes which have attics or crawl spaces because of their fabulous nesting conditions for such pests.

Here’s why roofs are attractive to rats:

  • Security from Predators: Rats feel safer in elevated places as these places are least liked to be hunted by predators like cats or larger birds.
  • Warmth: Roof spaces are warm, especially during cooler periods, so they make a perfect nesting ground.
  • Accessibility: Rats are excellent climbers and can scale walls or trees or pipes and reach the roofs. Gaps left by vents and loose tiles make them an easy entry point.
  • Food Sources: When food sources are nearby, rats will camp in your roof so they’ll not be far from their next meal.

How To Know If Rats Are Present In Your Roof?

Before calling the reinforcements, it will be a good idea to confirm first that rats are indeed living in your roof. Here are the signs of a rat infestation:

  • Scratching Sounds: one of the most common indicators are rustling, scurrying or chewing sounds, primarily at night when rats are most active.
  • Droppings: rat droppings tend to be found in hidden, inaccessible areas of the home such as corners, near food stores. Droppings are typically small, black, and torpedo-shaped.
  • Gnaw Marks: rats enjoy gnawing on wood, electrical cables, and insulation. So, if you have torn-up wires or chewed furniture, you can rest assured that you have a rat infestation.
  • Footprints or Grease Marks: Greasy marks and footprints by walls or along their travel paths are left by rats because of the oils from their fur. Also, in dusty areas, you can find small footprints or even tail drag marks.
  • Nesting Materials: Rats use soft materials in making their nests, which may include insulation, paper, and cloth. Shredded materials under your roof or attic mean that rats are present.

Dangers of Having Rats in Roof

Having rats in the roof presents several problems:

  • Health Hazards: The rats are diseases, lepto hantavirus, and salmonella. These can easily be transmitted to man through contact with rat droppings or urine.
  • Structural Damage: Rats gnaw everything including wooden beams, pipes, wiring, and insulation which increases the risk of a fire. Rats have even damaged insulation, pipes, and wooden beams.
  • Rapid Reproduction: One pair of rats can reproduce very fast. Within three months, you would have a full-blown infestation if it is not addressed early on.
How to Eliminate Rats from Your Roof?

Getting rid of rats in the roof requires step by step handling. Here are the most effective ways of getting rid of them:

  1. Inspect and Seal Entry Points: Dealing with a rat infestation involves proceeding through the first step of identifying and sealing entry points they may be using to gain access to your roof. Common entry points include the following:
  • Gaps between roofing tiles or shingles
  • Broken or damaged vents
  • Holes around pipes or wiring
  • Cracks in walls or foundations

Cover up the gaps with metal wool, caulking or metal screen, as they will chew through softer materials like wood or plastic. Make sure every hole bigger than 6mm is covered up because rats can squeeze into surprisingly small openings.

  1. Eliminate Attraction Sites: This animal is attracted to those places with easy access to food and water. The removal of these attractants will make your home less desirable. Tips include the following:
  • Secure Trash Bins: All trash bins should have tight-fitting lids.
  • Clean Up Food Waste: Avoid leaving food scraps or leftover pet food outdoors.
  • Trim bushes: Flailing branches or vines may be a means of rat ladders to access your roof. Keep them trimmed back to eliminate easy entry points.
  • Store Food: At home, store food in sealed containers and do not let there be any open food left for rats.
  1. Set Traps: Once the entry points are sealed and all means of food have been removed, you can start trapping the rats that remain inside your roof. There are different types of traps, which include:
  • Snap Traps: These are the classic type. They snap shut when triggered by the rat. It is fast and humane if properly used.
  • Live Traps: If you do not want to kill the rats, live traps can catch them alive for you to release in a far area from your home.
  • Electronic Traps: These traps utilize a little electrical shock that kills the rat instantly. Effective and reused.Place the traps against walls or in areas where you’ve seen signs of rat activities. You can bait the trap with foods such as peanut butter, cheese, or nuts to attract the rats.
  1. Handling Rodenticides By Caution: Rodenticides, or rat poisons, can indeed work, but one uses them at a time with caution, especially around pets and small children. They take several days to start working, during which rats may die in hard-to-reach areas of your roof: possible sources of unpleasant odors or even health hazards. If you decide to use rodenticides, it is best to have a professional pest control service do the handling.
  2. Professional Pest Control Services : Rat infestation can indeed turn out to be one real challenge, especially if the infestation is really severe. Hiring professional pest control services would therefore turn out to be a much better option. 7 State Pest Control in Melbourne specializes in pest control for rats. The company equips clients with very effective methods that easily get rid of infestations.

Pest control experts can assess the situation, employ high-tech machinery, and safely target specific treatments to eliminate rats from your roof. They also work to make sure that the infestation does not come back by providing preventive measures and long-term solutions.

Preventing Return of Rats

After eliminating rats from your roof, preventing its recurrence is an important task. Some of the long-term preventive measures include:

Inspect regularly: go through your roof and attic time to time to look for signs of rats or new entry points.

  • Keep your estate clean: trim the shrubs and other plants, patch all cracks or holes in your roof, and clean your gutters.
  • Install rat barriers: Install rat guards along pipes and tree trunks that lead to your roof.

Even though the rats in the roof can pose a serious matter, proper approach will help you remove them and prevent return. Sealing the entry points, trapping them, removal of attractants, and calling for professional intervention when need be is what can help your house stay rat-free. posts.title: How to Make Your Melbourne Home Wasp-Free: 7 Proven Prevention Tips
posts.excerpt: In Melbourne, wasps are more than just an occasional backyard nuisance. They are a frequent problem, particularly from late spring through early autumn when the warmer weather encourages them to become more active.  With plenty of food sources and nesting spots in suburban gardens, outdoor eating areas, and roof spaces,
posts.content_html:
In Melbourne, wasps are more than just an occasional backyard nuisance. They are a frequent problem, particularly from late spring through early autumn when the warmer weather encourages them to become more active. 

With plenty of food sources and nesting spots in suburban gardens, outdoor eating areas, and roof spaces, wasps can quickly turn your peaceful home into a risky environment.

The problem with wasps isn’t only that they are annoying. 

They can be aggressive when threatened, delivering painful stings that may lead to severe allergic reactions in some people. 

Pets are also at risk if they try to chase or bite a wasp. Beyond health concerns, a wasp infestation can make it uncomfortable or even unsafe to enjoy your garden, balcony, or patio.

Removing an established wasp nest can be dangerous and is best left to professionals. That’s why prevention is both safer and more cost-effective than dealing with a full infestation. 

In this blog , you’ll find practical steps to keep your property safe, along with advice on when to seek expert help for wasp nest control Melbourne services.

Why Wasp Control is Essential in Melbourne

Melbourne’s climate creates the perfect environment for wasps to thrive. They become most active in spring and summer, building nests and searching for food. 

The European wasp, one of the most aggressive species, is especially common in the area, along with paper wasps and mud daubers.

There are several important reasons to keep wasps under control:

  • Health risks: Wasp stings are painful and can cause swelling, redness, and in severe cases, anaphylaxis.
  • Pet safety: Dogs and cats may get stung if they disturb a nest or chase wasps.
  • Property disruption: A nest near a doorway, roof eave, or garden can make those areas unsafe to use.

For these reasons, regular monitoring and preventive measures are essential for keeping your home and family safe.

Tip 1: Keep Food Sources Covered

One of the main reasons wasps come near homes is food. They are drawn to sweet and protein-rich foods, making outdoor meals, rubbish bins, and even pet bowls potential targets.

To reduce their interest:

  • Keep food covered during outdoor picnics or barbecues.
  • Store pet food indoors when it’s not being eaten.
  • Close and secure compost bins.

By removing easy access to food, you make your property less appealing to wasps and reduce the chance of them hanging around.

Tip 2: Seal Entry Points Around the Home

Wasps often look for sheltered places to build nests, such as wall cavities, roof spaces, and under eaves. Even small gaps can be enough for them to get inside.

To prevent this:

  • Check around windows, doors, and rooflines for openings.
  • Install fine mesh screens over vents.
  • Use sealant to close cracks in walls and gaps in timber.

Doing this in early spring is particularly useful because it prevents wasps from starting a nest in the first place.

Tip 3: Maintain Your Garden Regularly

A messy or overgrown garden can be very inviting to wasps. Dense shrubs, tall grass, and fallen fruit can all encourage them to settle nearby.

Good garden maintenance includes:

  • Pruning trees, hedges, and bushes.
  • Removing fallen fruit and flowers promptly.
  • Clearing away piles of wood, leaves, or debris where wasps might hide.

Not only does this make your yard look tidier, but it also removes many potential nesting spots.

Tip 4: Avoid Strong Fragrances Outdoors

Wasps are sensitive to smell and are attracted to certain scents, including perfumes, scented body sprays, and some types of flowers.

If you plan to spend time outdoors:

  • Avoid wearing strong fragrances.
  • Choose unscented candles instead of heavily perfumed ones.
  • Be aware that bright, floral patterns can also attract them.

By reducing scent-based attraction, you make your outdoor spaces less interesting to wasps.

Tip 5: Secure Outdoor Rubbish Bins

Rubbish bins are one of the biggest wasp attractants, especially if they contain food scraps. If wasps find your bin, they’ll return regularly.

Prevent this by:

  • Using bins with tight-fitting lids.
  • Rinsing bins often to remove food smells.
  • Storing bins away from main doors and windows.

A clean, sealed bin is much less likely to become a wasp hotspot.

Tip 6: Install Wasp Deterrents

If you live in an area with frequent wasp problems, deterrents can help prevent nesting.

Common deterrents include:

  • Fake wasp nests: Since wasps are territorial, they often avoid areas where they think another colony exists. 
  • Natural repellents: Essential oils such as peppermint and clove may work as mild repellents. 
  • Traps: These can help reduce numbers but should be placed away from areas where people gather.

While deterrents can help, they are not a guaranteed solution and won’t remove an existing nest. For active nests, professional wasp nest control Melbourne services are recommended.

Tip 7: Schedule Regular Professional Inspections

Even with all the right prevention measures, wasps can sometimes find a way to build a nest on your property. Professional inspections can catch problems early before they become a serious risk.

An expert inspection can:

  • Identify wasp activity you may have missed.
  • Safely remove small nests before they grow.
  • Offer tailored prevention advice for your property.

Many homeowners choose an annual inspection to stay ahead of potential infestations.

When to Call a Professional for Wasp Nest Removal

There are times when professional help is the safest option. You should call an expert if:

  • You see a large, active wasp nest.
  • Wasps are swarming in a particular area.
  • You or a family member has a known allergy to stings.

DIY nest removal can be dangerous, particularly with aggressive species like European wasps. Professionals have the training, equipment, and safety procedures needed to remove nests effectively without putting you at risk.

Wasps are a common issue in Melbourne, but they don’t have to become a danger in your home. 

By keeping food covered, sealing entry points, maintaining your garden, avoiding strong fragrances, securing bins, using deterrents, and arranging professional inspections, you can significantly reduce the risk of infestation.

Taking action early is always safer and cheaper than dealing with a large, established nest. 

Taking early action is the best way to avoid the risks and costs of a large wasp infestation.

The Wasp Nest Problem

It’s necessary to know first what type of wasp it is as there are those types of wasps that are considered dangerous as opposed to others.

posts.content_html:
Melbourne has seen increasing wasp activity over the past few years, and experts predict that 2026 will bring an even larger rise in infestations. Warmer winters across Victoria have allowed more queens to survive, leading to earlier nesting and larger colonies by mid-summer. 

This means residents may encounter active nests far sooner than expected.

More homeowners searching for wasp nest Melbourne information are discovering that early detection and professional removal are becoming essential. A growing number of suburbs — including Point Cook, Cranbourne, Doncaster, Werribee, Melton, Craigieburn, Narre Warren, and beyond — have reported heightened wasp presence.

Early action is critical. Leaving a nest untreated increases risks, property damage, and aggressive behaviour, especially during the peak summer months. 

That’s why many Melbourne residents now opt for professional removal services rather than attempting risky DIY methods.

Understanding Wasp Behaviour: Why They Build Nests Near Homes

To better understand why wasp nest Melbourne cases are increasing, it helps to know how local wasps behave. Melbourne commonly encounters European wasps and paper wasps — both of which prefer sheltered, warm spaces close to human activity.

Wasps build nests near homes for several reasons:

  • Ready access to food sources such as meat scraps, fallen fruit, compost, and pet bowls
  • Shelter provided by wall voids, roofing, sheds, and backyard structures
  • A stable environment to raise their colony

Suburbs with larger blocks, gardens, and outdoor entertaining areas often experience more wasp activity due to these attractants. Once a queen identifies a suitable spot, the nest develops rapidly.

Fascinating and Lesser-Known Facts About Wasps

Including key facts helps Melbourne readers better understand the seriousness of a wasp nest Melbourne infestation:

  • Wasps are capable of recognising and remembering human faces.
  • A large European wasp nest can reach more than 10,000 wasps by late summer.
  • Wasps never reuse old nests; they build new ones every season.
  • European wasps may travel up to 500 metres when searching for food.
  • Wasps are natural predators and help reduce pests like caterpillars and spiders.
  • Their aggression spikes between February and March when food becomes scarce.

These facts highlight how quickly nests can grow and why professional removal is critical.

How to Identify a Wasp Nest in Melbourne Homes

One advantage of early detection is that a small nest is significantly easier and safer to handle. Look for early indicators such as:

  • A humming or buzzing sound from one side of the home
  • Wasps flying in repeated straight paths
  • Chewed wood fibres on fences and deck posts
  • Increasing wasp activity around bins and outdoor food sources

Typical nesting locations include:

  • Roof eaves
  • Sheds
  • Garages
  • Pergolas
  • Wall cavities
  • BBQ areas
  • Under house decking

Paper Wasps vs European Wasps

Paper wasps build small umbrella-shaped nests with open, exposed cells.
 European wasps create large enclosed structures resembling layered paper.

Identifying the right species is important because European wasps create the largest and most aggressive wasp nest Melbourne infestations.

Why DIY Wasp Nest Removal Is Dangerous 

With warmer summers predicted in 2026, wasp behaviour is expected to become more aggressive. Attempting DIY removal is extremely risky because:

  • Wasps defend their nest fiercely
  • Disturbing the nest releases alarm pheromones that trigger swarm attacks
  • Multiple stings can lead to severe allergic reactions
  • Fire, water, or supermarket sprays often make the situation worse
  • Hidden nests may be larger than they appear

A wasp nest Melbourne incident handled incorrectly can escalate in seconds. Without the right equipment or experience, DIY methods can quickly become dangerous.

Safe Steps Before a Professional Arrives

If you notice a nest on your property, these steps can help reduce risk:

  • Do not hit or spray the nest
  • Keep children and pets indoors
  • Avoid shining outdoor lights at night
  • Do not block wasp entry points
  • Keep food waste secure
  • Do not stand on unstable ladders or attempt to access high areas

These actions help ensure the nest remains undisturbed until a licensed technician can attend.

Professional Wasp Nest Removal in Melbourne: How Experts Handle It

Professional pest control teams use specialised techniques to remove nests safely. The process usually includes:

Inspection

A detailed assessment to locate the nest, identify the species, and determine the safest removal method.

Treatment Selection

Experts use approved products suitable for European or paper wasps. These treatments are designed to quickly neutralise the colony.

Safe Nest Removal

Protected gear, controlled application, and professional tools ensure safe removal without disturbing surrounding areas.

Aftercare

Sealing gaps, advising on food management, and preventing future infestations are part of the service.

Large, hidden, or aggressive nests must only be handled by licensed experts — especially during the height of summer when wasp nest Melbourne cases peak.

What Sets 7 States Pest Control Apart in 2026

  • Same-day service for many Melbourne suburbs
  • More than a decade of wasp removal experience

  • Emergency call-outs during high-activity months

The service focuses on precision, safety, and prompt solutions — essential qualities for managing wasp nest Melbourne situations.

Preventing Wasp Nests in 2026: Tips for Melbourne Homes

Prevention is always easier than removal. Homeowners can reduce wasp activity by:

  • Sealing small gaps around roofs and walls
  • Keeping bins closed and cleaned regularly
  • Removing fallen fruit and outdoor food scraps
  • Cleaning BBQ areas and outdoor kitchen spaces
  • Trimming overgrown shrubs and bushes
  • Inspecting roofs and gutters in spring
  • Scheduling annual pest inspections

These steps reduce the likelihood of a wasp nest Melbourne forming on your property.

When to Call a Professional Immediately

Immediate assistance is essential when:

Protect Your Home in 2026

Melbourne is expected to face increased wasp activity during the 2026 season due to climate changes and longer breeding cycles. Early detection, regular inspections, and safe removal are crucial for avoiding accidents and costly damage.

posts.title: How to Tell If Bed Bugs Are Gone: Post-Treatment Tips for Melbourne Homes
posts.excerpt: Finding bed bugs in your home is an unsettling experience.  For many Melbourne homeowners, it leads to sleepless nights, constant itching, and the stress of not knowing when or where they’ll show up again.  After finally calling in professional help, you expect peace of mind—but lingering doubts often remain. Even
posts.content_html:
Finding bed bugs in your home is an unsettling experience. 

For many Melbourne homeowners, it leads to sleepless nights, constant itching, and the stress of not knowing when or where they’ll show up again. 

After finally calling in professional help, you expect peace of mind—but lingering doubts often remain.

Even after professional bed bugs treatment in Melbourne, homeowners often wonder: are they really gone?

This kind of uncertainty is completely normal. 

Bed bugs are discreet pests, and their elimination doesn’t always bring immediate, visible proof. 

In this blog , we’ll walk you through what to expect after treatment, signs that indicate success, and how to avoid common mistakes.

What Happens After a Bed Bug Treatment?

Post-treatment, it’s important to remember that results are not always immediate. 

While your pest control technician may have eliminated most of the infestation, some activity may continue for a short time.

Here’s what typically happens:

  • Residual Activity: Most professional treatments use residual insecticides. This means that bed bugs emerging from hiding spots may still be alive initially but will soon die after exposure. 
  • Hidden Eggs: Bed bug eggs are small, often hidden deep in cracks, and may survive treatment. These can hatch within 7 to 14 days. 
  • Timeframe for Results: It can take up to 2 to 4 weeks for all signs of bed bugs to disappear completely.

Signs Bed Bugs Are Truly Gone

Wondering how to tell if the treatment worked? These are the key indicators that your bed bugs are gone:

No More Bites or Itching

If you’re no longer waking up with red, itchy welts, it’s a good sign that the infestation is under control.

No Live Bed Bugs or Shed Skins

Bed bugs leave behind their old skins as they mature. The absence of these around mattresses and bed frames is another encouraging signal.

No New Black Dots or Stains

Small black spots or rusty stains on your bedding, mattress seams, or furniture are signs of droppings. No new marks likely mean the pests are gone.

No Suspicious Nighttime Activity

A bed bug-free home is quiet—no crawling sensations, no new bites, and no visible insects.

Common Mistakes That Can Lead to False Alarms

Many homeowners mistake unrelated issues for a return of bed bugs. Here’s how to avoid unnecessary panic:

  • Confusing Other Insects: Carpet beetles, fleas, or mosquito bites can mimic bed bug symptoms. 
  • Reading Old Stains as New Activity: Leftover droppings or blood stains don’t necessarily mean the pests are still present. 
  • Reintroducing Infested Items Too Soon: Items like bedding or furniture that were removed before treatment may still contain eggs if not properly cleaned. 

Stay calm and focus on current signs, not what was left behind.

How to Confirm Bed Bug Elimination

If you’re still not sure whether the bed bugs are gone, here are some simple ways to check:

  • Use Bed Bug Traps: Put traps under the legs of your bed. If no bugs get caught after 2 to 4 weeks, that’s a good sign they’re gone.
  • Keep Checking: Look around your mattress, bed frame, and edges of the room for any signs of bugs.
  • Get a Professional to Check: A pest control expert can do a follow-up visit to confirm everything is clear using their special tools.
When to Consider a Follow-Up Treatment

Sometimes, a second treatment is necessary. You should consider follow-up services if:

  • You’re Still Seeing Live Bugs or Bites: Activity that continues more than two weeks after treatment may mean some bugs survived.
  • Baby Bed Bugs Show Up: If you start seeing tiny bed bugs (called nymphs), it might mean some eggs weren’t killed during the first treatment and have now hatched.
  • DIY Treatments Didn’t Work: If you tried to treat the issue on your own before calling professionals, some bugs may have been missed.

For larger or long-standing infestations, multiple treatments are often required for full control.

Tips to Stay Bed Bug-Free After Treatment

Once your home is clear, prevention is key. These simple steps can help keep bed bugs from coming back:

  • Use Mattress Covers: These special covers seal your mattress and stop any leftover bugs from getting out or new ones from getting in.

  • Vacuum Often: Focus on areas around your bed, walls, and soft furniture. 
  • Be Careful with Second-Hand Items: Always check used furniture or clothes before bringing them home. Treat them if needed.

posts.title: Keep Rodents From Making Your Home Their Home This Winter
posts.excerpt: As the days get colder and the nights grow longer, the cozy appeal of our homes isn’t just for us – it’s also attractive to unwanted guests: pests. Among these unwelcome visitors, rodents like mice and rats are particularly common during winter. Their natural instinct is to seek shelter from
posts.content_html:
As the days get colder and the nights grow longer, the cozy appeal of our homes isn’t just for us – it’s also attractive to unwanted guests: pests. Among these unwelcome visitors, rodents like mice and rats are particularly common during winter. Their natural instinct is to seek shelter from the harsh and unpredictable winter weather, and unfortunately, your warm and comfortable home can become an ideal haven for them.

But don’t worry, by taking some proactive steps including pest control services, you can keep your home rodent-free and enjoy your winter in peace.

Understanding Winter Pest Invasion

While the Australian winter is generally mild compared to colder climates, it still poses challenges for rodents seeking warmth and sustenance. This is why we see an increase in rodent activity during this season. Here’s what you need to understand about winter pest invasions:

  • Seeking Shelter: As mentioned earlier, rodents are driven to find warm and secure shelters during winter. They’ll actively search for any openings in your home, such as cracks in the foundation, gaps around pipes, or unsealed vents.
  • Food Source: Rodents need a reliable food source to survive the winter. Your home, with its readily available food scraps, crumbs, and pet food, becomes an attractive option for them. Additionally, overflowing bins, compost heaps, and accessible fruit trees near your house can attract them further.
  • Increased Activity: As the temperatures drop, rodents become more active in their search for shelter and food. You may notice increased noises in the walls or attic, droppings around your home, and even gnaw marks on furniture or wires.

5 Effective Ways To Keep Rodents Away From Your Home

Here are five effective steps you can take to keep rodents at bay this winter:

1. Seal Entry Points: Fortifying Your Home Against Unwanted Guests:

Imagine your home as a fortress. Your first line of defense is ensuring there are no sealing cracks, holes, or gaps around doors, windows, pipes, and foundation. Even a tiny opening can be enough for a determined rodent to squeeze through.

 

  • Inspect your home thoroughly: Look for potential entry points outside your house, paying close attention to areas around pipes, vents, and the foundation. Inside, check for gaps around doors, windows, and any other openings.
  • Seal the gaps: Use caulk to fill any cracks or holes you find. For larger openings, consider using steel wool or hardware cloth to create a barrier that rodents can’t chew through. Don’t forget to seal gaps around dryer vents and any holes in your chimney.

2. Trim Trees And Shrubs: Eliminating Rodent Access Points Near Your Home:

Rodents are skilled climbers and can use overhanging trees and shrubs as bridges to reach your roof and eventually gain access to your home. Here’s what you can do:

  • Keep trees and shrubs trimmed: Maintain a distance of at least six feet between tree branches and your roof. This will discourage rodents from using them as stepping stones.
  • Clear away debris: Remove any piles of leaves, branches, or other debris near your house. These can provide rodents with hiding places and make your home more attractive to them.

3. Store Food Properly: Removing Temptations For Hungry Invaders:

Rodents are always on the lookout for food, and any readily available sources will attract them to your home. Here are some tips:

  • Store food in airtight containers: This applies to all food items, including cereals, grains, pet food, and even snacks. Don’t leave food sitting out on counters or in open bags.
  • Clean up spills immediately: Spilled food crumbs or leftover scraps can be a feast for rodents. Clean up any messes quickly and thoroughly.
  • Empty your trash regularly: Take out your trash regularly, especially kitchen bins, and ensure they have tight-fitting lids. Don’t leave overflowing bins outside your house.

4. Decluttering: Creating An Environment Unfriendly To Uninvited Guests:

Rodents love clutter! It provides them with hiding places and nesting materials. Here’s what you can do:

  • De-clutter your home: This includes removing piles of clothes, newspapers, boxes, or anything else that creates potential hiding spots for rodents.
  • Organize your storage areas: Keep basements, attics, and garages organized to eliminate potential rodent havens.
  • Store items properly: Don’t store cardboard boxes directly on the floor. Use shelves or place them on plastic containers to elevate them from the ground.

5. Install Door Sweeps And Screens: Adding Extra Layers Of Protection Against Rodents:

Door sweeps and screens offer an extra layer of protection against rodents. Here’s what you can do:

  • Install door sweeps: These sweep the floor as the door opens and closes, creating a barrier that prevents rodents from entering through the gap beneath the door.
  • Use window screens: Ensure all your windows have properly fitted screens to prevent rodents from entering through open windows.

Additional Tips:

  • Consider setting humane traps indoors to catch any rodents that manage to get inside. However, remember to check and dispose of trapped rodents regularly.
  • If you have a fireplace, ensure the chimney flue is properly sealed when not in use.
  • Maintain your landscaping by trimming overgrown bushes and trees away from your house. This eliminates potential hiding places for rodents near your home.

Best Tools and Products for Keeping Rodents Away This Winter

Seal Up Your Fortress

Rodents are incredibly resourceful and can squeeze through surprisingly tiny gaps. Your first line of defence is to seal up any potential entry points. This includes:

 

  • Cracks and gaps: Inspect your foundation, walls, windows, and doors for any cracks or crevices larger than a quarter-inch. Use caulk or weather stripping to seal these up.
  • Vents and openings: Cover vents with hardware cloth to allow air circulation while preventing rodents from entering.
  • Pipes and utility lines: Check where pipes and utilities enter your home and seal any gaps around them with caulk or expanding foam.
  • Doors and windows: Ensure doors and windows close tightly without any gaps. Replace any damaged weather stripping or worn-out door sweeps.

Clean Up Your Food Sources:

  • Store food properly: Keep all food items, including pet food, in airtight containers made of glass or metal.
  • Clean up spills immediately: Don’t leave crumbs or food debris lying around,as even small amounts can attract rodents.
  • Manage your garbage: Use bins with tight-fitting lids and empty them regularly.

Eliminate Hiding Places:

  • Trim landscaping: Keep shrubs, bushes, and trees trimmed back at least 18 inches from your house. This removes potential hiding spots close to your entry points.
  • Store firewood properly: Stack firewood away from your house and off the ground.
  • Declutter your home: Avoid creating piles of clutter in your basement, attic,or garage, as these can provide nesting areas for rodents.

Utilize Repellents:

  • Natural rodent repellents: Peppermint, eucalyptus, and cayenne pepper oils are known to have rodent-repelling properties:
    • Dilute a few drops of essential oil in water and spray around potential entry points.
    • Place cotton balls soaked in these oils strategically throughout your home.
  • Commercial repellents: Consider using commercially available rodenticides or ultrasonic repellents. Always follow the manufacturer’s instructions carefully to ensure safe and effective use.

Traps

If you suspect a rodent infestation, consider setting traps. However, be aware that traps are not a long-term solution and should be used in conjunction with other preventative measures.

Remember: When dealing with an existing rodent infestation, it’s important to seek professional help from a licensed pest control company. They have the expertise and resources to safely and effectively eliminate the problem and prevent future infestations.

Conclusion

Imagine this: crackling fire, warm blankets, a steaming cup of your favourite beverage – the perfect picture of a cosy winter evening. Now imagine sharing this scene with unwelcome guests: scurrying rodents, gnawed wires, and the constant worry of disease. By taking the necessary steps outlined above, you can turn your vision of a delightful winter into a reality.

However, prevention is always better than cure. Don’t wait until you hear scratching noises in the attic or see droppings in the corner. Take action now to keep your home rodent-free and enjoy a peaceful, pest-free winter.

But what if you’re already facing a rodent problem?

Don’t worry; help is readily available. At 7 States Pest Control, we understand the stress and frustration associated with pest infestations. Our experienced and licensed professionals can provide comprehensive pest control services solutions tailored to your specific needs. We offer a range of safe and effective methods to eliminate existing rodent problems and prevent future infestations.

Contact us today for consultation in Melbourne and quote. Let us help you reclaim your home and enjoy a pest-free winter wonderland!

posts.content_html:
Spiders are a common sight in many Melbourne homes, but when they start multiplying or nesting indoors, they can quickly turn from nuisance to nightmare. While most spiders are harmless, their presence can be unsettling — especially when they start appearing in bathrooms, kitchens, or kids’ rooms. 

If you’re constantly reaching for a tissue or vacuum cleaner, it might be time to consider a more effective solution.

This blog will walk you through everything you need to know about spider pest control in Melbourne — including common species, why infestations occur, and what you can do to protect your space.

Why Spider Infestations Happen in Melbourne

Melbourne’s weather and mix of city and suburbs make it a great place for spiders to live. When it gets cold or very humid, spiders often come inside looking for warmth and shelter. 

That’s why you might see more spiders in your home during winter or rainy days. They usually hide in quiet places like corners, ceilings, or garages.

Common causes of spider infestations include:

  • Messy areas inside or outside the house
  • Lots of insects around (spiders eat other bugs)
  • Small cracks or open gaps in walls and windows
  • Overgrown gardens or untidy sheds

Types of Spiders Found in Melbourne Homes

Knowing the types of spiders you might find at home in Melbourne helps you understand which ones are harmless and which need attention. 

Some spiders can be dangerous, while most are harmless and actually help by eating other pests.

Common species include:

  • Redback Spiders: These spiders have a venomous bite and a clear red stripe on their back.
  • White-Tailed Spiders: They are often found inside homes, hiding in clothes and bedding.
  • Huntsman Spiders: These spiders are big but not aggressive. They can look scary but usually don’t harm people.
  • Daddy Long Legs: These are harmless spiders that you might see in large groups, usually in quiet corners.

DIY Methods for Spider Control

Many people try to get rid of spiders themselves using DIY methods. These might include using sprays, homemade traps, or cleaning up spider webs regularly. While these steps can give some quick relief, they often don’t fix the problem completely.

Challenges with DIY methods:

  • It’s hard to find all the places where spiders hide, like cracks or behind furniture.
  • Some sprays or chemicals bought from stores may not be strong enough to stop the spiders for good.
  • Using chemicals without proper knowledge can be risky for children, pets, and even the environment.
  • DIY methods usually only remove visible spiders but don’t stop new ones from coming in.
  • Without sealing entry points like cracks and gaps, spiders can easily return.
  • Some spiders are more dangerous and need special treatment that only professionals know how to do safely.

Why Professional Spider Pest Control Is the Smart Choice

DIY methods might offer temporary relief, but professional pest control ensures the root of the problem is addressed. Expert technicians know where spiders hide, what attracts them, and how to apply treatments safely and effectively.

Benefits of hiring professionals:

  • They use treatments made just for the spiders found in Melbourne.
  • Their methods are safe for your family, pets, and the environment.
  • They help stop spiders from coming back for a long time.
  • They check your home and seal up cracks and gaps where spiders can get in.
What to Expect from a Spider Control Treatment

If you’re noticing spiders in and around your home, getting professional help can be the best way to handle the problem. 

Spider control services use expert knowledge and safe treatments to remove spiders and help stop them from coming back. 

Here’s what usually happens when you book a spider pest control service:

  • Initial inspection: The technician will carefully check your home for signs of spiders, such as webs, egg sacs, or sightings. They will also look for places where spiders can enter your home, like cracks, gaps, or open windows.
  • Treatment plan: After the inspection, a plan is made that fits the type of spiders you have and how bad the problem is. This plan targets the right areas and uses the best methods for your situation.
  • Application: Safe and effective insecticides or treatments are applied to places where spiders like to hide or travel. These spots include roof spaces, garages, under furniture, window frames, and other quiet corners. The products used are selected to be safe for your family and pets while effectively controlling spiders.
  • Prevention tips: The technician will give you advice on how to keep spiders away in the future. This might include tips like keeping your home tidy, removing clutter, sealing cracks, and reducing insect food sources for spiders.
  • Follow-up visits: Some services offer follow-up checks to make sure the treatment worked well and to do extra treatment if needed. This helps keep your home spider-free over time.

By knowing what to expect, you can be more confident that the professionals will handle your spider problem safely and thoroughly.

Tips to Keep Spiders Out of Your Melbourne Home

While professional treatment is essential for existing infestations, regular maintenance can help keep spiders at bay.

Practical spider prevention tips:

  • Seal gaps: Close any cracks or openings around windows and doors.
  • Clear clutter: Keep garages, sheds, and corners clean and tidy.
  • Turn off lights: Lights can attract bugs, which spiders come to eat.
  • Use natural oils: Eucalyptus or peppermint oil can help keep spiders away.
  • Vacuum often: Clean places like corners, ceilings, and under furniture regularly.

Is Spider Pest Control Safe for Kids and Pets?

Yes, spider pest control is generally safe for children and pets—especially when done by professionals. 

Safety is very important, especially in homes with little kids, babies, dogs, or cats. 

Most pest control companies in Melbourne use low-tox sprays or treatments that are designed to be safe for families.

The sprays are only harmful when they are wet. 

That’s why you may be asked to leave the house for a few hours during and after the treatment. This gives time for the spray to dry properly and keeps everyone safe.

Here’s what you can do to stay safe:

  • Keep kids and pets out of treated areas until everything is dry.
  • Follow the technician’s instructions carefully.
  • Clean and store away food, toys, and pet bowls before the treatment.
  • Open windows and let fresh air in once you’re back home.

When you hire a professional, they will explain everything clearly and make sure your home is treated in a safe and careful way.

 

Choosing the Right Spider Pest Control Service in Melbourne

When selecting a pest control provider, look for:

  • Licensed and insured technicians
  • Local experience with Melbourne pests
  • Transparent pricing with no hidden costs
  • Good customer reviews and satisfaction guarantees

Don’t Let Spiders Take Over Your Home

Spiders might seem like a small problem, but if you ignore them, they can quickly spread and become a bigger issue. 

Whether you’ve seen a few around your home or you’re dealing with a serious infestation, it’s important to act early.

For reliable and safe spider pest control in Melbourne, 7 States Pest Control is your trusted local expert.

Their trained experts know how to remove spiders and keep them from coming back—using family- and pet-safe methods that work. 

You’ll get a professional inspection, targeted treatment, and helpful tips to prevent future problems

Based in Melbourne, 7 States Pest Control is a trusted name when it comes to safe and effective spider removal. 

Their team has years of experience handling all types of spider problems—from Redbacks to Huntsmans—using professional treatments that are tough on pests but safe for families and pets..

posts.content_html:
Melbourne is a city known for its beautiful landscapes, vibrant culture, and diverse wildlife. However, with this natural beauty comes the challenge of dealing with pests, and one of the most problematic pests in the city is the wasp. Wasps are particularly aggressive during the warmer months, and their presence can pose a significant risk to people, pets, and properties. If you live in Melbourne, especially in suburbs that are rich in greenery and open spaces, you may already be aware of the wasp problem.

At 7 States Pest Control, we understand the frustration and danger of dealing with wasps. Our expert team is here to provide safe and efficient Wasp Nest Removal Melbourne services, helping you reclaim your outdoor spaces and protect your loved ones from these aggressive insects. But first, let’s explore the suburbs that are most commonly affected by wasp infestations and why professional pest control is crucial in these areas.

Suburbs with High Wasp Activity in Melbourne

1.Yarra Valley:

 

Known for its stunning vineyards and lush landscapes, Yarra Valley is a beautiful area, but it’s also a hotspot for wasps. The abundance of gardens and outdoor spaces creates ideal conditions for wasps to build their nests. If you live in or around Yarra Valley, it’s essential to keep an eye out for wasp activity, especially during the summer months.

 

2.Mornington Peninsula:



The Mornington Peninsula is another popular area that faces significant wasp issues. Its coastal location, combined with numerous gardens and parks, makes it a prime target for wasps. Residents and visitors alike often experience wasp problems during outdoor activities, making professional pest control services a necessity.

 

 

3. Dandenong Ranges:



With its dense forests and vast parks, the Dandenong Ranges is a picturesque area, but it’s also highly susceptible to wasp infestations. Wasps often build their nests in trees or roof spaces, posing a threat to both residents and tourists. If you notice wasp activity in this area, it’s important to seek Wasp Nest Removal Melbourne services as soon as possible.

 

 

4. Bayside Suburbs (Brighton, Sandringham, Hampton):



The Bayside suburbs, including Brighton, Sandringham, and Hampton, are known for their beautiful beaches and vibrant communities. However, wasps are also a common problem in these areas, especially in gardens and near outdoor dining spaces. Residents in these coastal suburbs should be vigilant about checking for wasp nests around their properties.

 

 

5. Eastern Suburbs (Doncaster, Templestowe, Blackburn):


The eastern suburbs of Melbourne, such as Doncaster, Templestowe, and Blackburn, are home to many large residential properties with gardens, making them attractive to wasps. These suburbs are frequently targeted by wasps looking for food and shelter, and nest removal is often necessary to keep residents safe.

Nillumbik and Eltham are semi-rural areas with plenty of trees and greenery, providing a perfect environment for wasps. These suburbs are prone to wasp infestations, and professional pest control is often required to remove nests safely and effectively.

 

 

 

Why Are Melbourne Suburbs So Wasp-Prone?

Several factors contribute to the prevalence of wasps in Melbourne suburbs:

  • Climate: Melbourne’s temperate climate, with its warm summers and mild winters, provides ideal conditions for wasp populations to thrive.
  • Abundant Food Sources: The city’s lush gardens, parks, and fruit trees offer a plentiful supply of food for wasps, attracting them to residential areas.
  • Ideal Nesting Sites: Many Melbourne homes and buildings have features that provide suitable nesting locations for wasps, such as eaves, attics, and cavities in walls.

Why Are Wasps Such a Problem?

Wasps are not only annoying; they can be dangerous. Unlike bees, wasps are aggressive and can sting multiple times without dying. This makes them a significant threat to anyone who gets too close to their nest. Additionally, wasp stings can cause severe allergic reactions in some individuals, which can be life-threatening if not treated promptly.

Wasps are particularly active during the warmer months, as this is when they are building nests and foraging for food. Common food sources for wasps include sugary drinks, fruits, and food scraps, which is why they are often found around outdoor dining areas or picnics. Wasps are also attracted to flowers and plants, making gardens a prime location for nests.

The Importance of Professional Wasp Nest Removal

Attempting to remove a wasp nest on your own is not only dangerous but can also make the problem worse. Wasps are highly territorial, and disturbing their nest can cause them to swarm and attack. This is why professional Wasp Nest Removal Melbourne services are essential for safely and effectively removing wasp nests from your property.

Our team of experts is trained to handle wasp infestations of all sizes, from small nests in gardens to large nests in roof spaces. posts.content_html:
Have you ever spotted a nasty wasp near your home and immediately grabbed a can of bug spray from the cupboard? You are definitely not alone. Most people try to handle wasps themselves, but they are missing out on the full potential of professional pest control methods.

 A simple grocery store spray rarely solves the root of the problem. In fact, without the right Melbourne wasp removal techniques, you might just make the whole swarm angry. 

Today, we are opening our toolbox to share the secret “hacks” that professional exterminators use to keep your home safe, sting-free, and clear of wasps for good.

Why Most Homeowners Fail at DIY Wasp Control

People often think getting rid of wasps is as simple as pointing an aerosol can and running away. But stinging insects, especially European wasps, are smart, highly organized, and very aggressive when threatened.

When you try to remove them without the right tools or knowledge, you usually miss the hidden nests buried deep inside your wall cavities, roof voids, or underground in your garden. If you don’t use expert Melbourne wasp removal, you might successfully kill a few of the worker wasps flying around, but you leave the queen safely hidden inside the nest. That means the colony will just keep laying eggs and growing. To truly fix the problem, you need to use the hidden tricks of the trade.

10 Hidden “Features” of Pro Wasp Control You Didn’t Know About

1. Red-Light Night Eradication

What it does: Allows exterminators to sneak up on a dangerous nest at night without triggering an attack. 

How it works: Wasps have a very specific range of vision and they cannot easily process red light. We wait until the sun completely goes down, which is when all the wasps are asleep inside the nest. Then, our technicians use special red-filtered torches to see exactly what we are doing without waking up the colony. 

Use case: This is the perfect hack for safely treating a massive, exposed nest right above your front door without causing a dangerous swarm to attack your family.

2. Deep Cavity Dusting

What it does: Reaches nests hidden deep inside your walls where normal liquid sprays simply cannot go. 

How it works: Instead of using wet sprays that can ruin your plasterboard and cause water damage, we use a specialized pressure pump. This tool pushes dry, insecticidal dust through tiny cracks in your brickwork or siding. The wasps then carry this dust right into the heart of the nest on their legs and bodies. 

Use case: When you can hear a loud scratching and buzzing sound behind your bedroom wall, but you cannot actually see a hole or a nest.

3. Flight Path Tracking

What it does: Helps us find the exact location of a hidden nest just by watching how the bugs fly in the air. 

How it works: Expert Melbourne wasp removal technicians do not just wander around hoping to stumble upon a nest. We follow the “busy” workers. When a wasp is carrying food or wood back home, it flies in a straight, heavy, and direct line. We simply follow that invisible flight path straight back to their hidden door. 

Use case: Finding a dangerous underground European wasp nest hidden under the dirt in your large backyard garden.

4. Pheromone Scrubbing

What it does: Stops new wasps from moving into the old, empty nest space next season. 

How it works: When wasps die or leave a nest, they leave a strong chemical scent (called a pheromone) behind. We treat the area to completely wipe out this invisible smell. This ensures that other passing wasps do not smell the old nest, get curious, and start a brand new colony in the exact same spot. 

Use case: Preventing wasps from returning to the same comfortable gap in your roof year after year.

5. The Queen Target System

What it does: Destroys the whole colony from the inside out by taking out the leader. 

How it works: If you only swat and kill the worker wasps flying outside, the queen just lays more eggs to replace them. Our treatments are specifically designed to be slow-acting enough to be carried back to the queen. Once she is gone, the entire colony collapses and dies off completely. 

Use case: Ending a severe, ongoing wasp problem that keeps coming back to bother you every single summer.

6. Thermal Imaging Scanners

What it does: Lets us practically “see” right through your solid walls to find the heat coming from a busy wasp nest. 

How it works: A nest full of thousands of moving wasps generates a lot of body heat. We use a high-tech thermal camera to scan your inside walls. A glowing hot spot on the camera screen tells us exactly where the nest is located so we know exactly where to treat. 

Use case: Spotting a nest inside a solid brick wall without having to blindly knock down any expensive bricks.

7. Botanical Eco-Treatments

What it does: Kills the stinging insects quickly but stays safe for your family, pets, and garden. 

How it works: We use smart treatments made from natural plant extracts, like pyrethrin found in chrysanthemum flowers. It is incredibly deadly to wasps, but it breaks down very fast when exposed to natural sunlight, leaving no long-term toxic residue behind in your yard. 

Use case: Performing safe melbourne wasp removal in a backyard where dogs, cats, and young kids play every single day.

8. Weep-Hole Exclusion Meshing

What it does: Blocks wasps from getting inside your home’s brick walls in the first place.

 How it works: After we remove a nest from your wall, we can install special, custom-fit stainless-steel meshes over your weep holes (the tiny vertical gaps built into your brickwork). This allows your house to breathe so air can get in, but wasps and spiders are locked out for good. 

Use case: Securing a newly built home from future pest invasions before they even happen.

9. High-Powered Vacuum Extraction

What it does: Sucks up wasps instantly without using any chemical sprays at all. 

How it works: We use a heavy-duty, heavily filtered pest vacuum to literally suck the angry wasps right out of the air and out of the nest. This is a purely physical removal method that captures them safely inside a sealed chamber. 

Use case: Removing a nest inside a kitchen, cafe, or food-prep area where chemical sprays are strictly not allowed.

10. Total Containment Suits

What it does: Keeps the exterminator 100% safe, which means they can get close enough to do the job right the first time. 

How it works: Our team wears thick, professional-grade sting-proof bee suits. Because our technicians are completely protected from head to toe, we don’t have to panic or rush. We can take our time to carefully remove every piece of the nest without leaving anything behind.

 Use case: Handling highly aggressive swarms that are ready to attack anyone who comes near their home.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Blocking the entrance hole: Never plug a hole with expanding foam or tape where wasps are flying in. They will panic, chew through your soft inside plasterboard walls, and end up swarming in your living room.
  • Spraying during the heat of the day: Wasps are wide awake, fast, and very angry in the bright sun. This is the absolute worst time to try a DIY spray attack.
  • Using a normal flashlight at night: Shining a bright white torch at a nest in the dark will make the wasps fly straight up the beam of light and right into your face. Always leave it to a Melbourne wasp removal pro who has a red light.

Pro Tips to Get Better Results

  • Check your yard in early spring: Try to catch the queen while she is alone building a tiny, golf-ball-sized nest. It is so much easier to remove a tiny nest early on than a massive one in January.
  • Keep your rubbish bins tightly sealed: European wasps are scavengers. They love leftover meat, pet food, and sweet sugary drinks. A tight lid on your outdoor rubbish bin keeps them away from your property.
  • Call the pros early: The very moment you see a steady line of yellow and black insects flying into a gap in your house, call for professional Melbourne wasp removal. Do not wait a month for the nest to grow to the size of a basketball.

FAQ

  1. How much does Melbourne wasp removal cost? 

The exact price depends on where the nest is hidden and how big the colony has grown. However, fixing it early with a professional is always much cheaper than repairing expensive wall damage after the wasps chew through your plaster!

  1. Is it safe to just leave a wasp nest alone in winter? 

Sometimes standard paper wasps die off in the cold winter. But European wasps in Australia often survive the mild cold and their nests just keep growing year after year. It is always best to have it removed.

  1. Will the wasps come back to the exact same spot? 

Not if you use an expert pest controller. We use pheromone scrubbing to remove their unique scent, so new bugs won’t even know the old nest was ever there.

  1. Are your pest treatments safe for my dog? 

Yes! A professional Melbourne wasp removal service uses highly targeted, eco-friendly dusts and sprays. Once the treatment has settled and dried, it is totally safe for your furry friends to go back into the yard.

Dealing with stinging insects is a scary situation for any homeowner, but you really do not have to do it alone or rely on weak supermarket bug sprays. 

By taking advantage of the hidden tricks of the trade—like thermal imaging cameras, red-light night treatments, and smart deep-cavity dusting—the pros can clear out your pest problem quickly, safely, and permanently.

That is exactly where 7 States Pest Control comes in. As a trusted, fully licensed local team, we pride ourselves on protecting local families and businesses from dangerous pests. 

Whether you are facing a massive nest of stinging insects or need reliable rodent pest control Melbourne residents can count on to stop a rat and mice infestation, we have you completely covered. We combine years of hands-on experience with advanced, eco-friendly treatments that are tough on pests but completely safe for your children and pets. 

We combine years of hands-on experience with advanced, eco-friendly treatments that are tough on stinging insects but completely safe for your children and pets. 

We don’t just spray the bugs you can see; we take the time to track down the hidden queens, neutralize the nests, and eliminate the problem at its true source so they don’t come back.

posts.excerpt: In recent years, Melbourne has witnessed an alarming increase in bed bug infestations. posts.content_html:
In recent years, Melbourne has witnessed an alarming increase in bed bug infestations. These resilient pests, once thought to be a thing of the past, are now thriving in many homes across the city. 

With modern travel, high-density living, and shared spaces, it’s no surprise that these creatures are finding more opportunities to spread.

Bed bugs are not only a nuisance but also a health risk, causing discomfort and sleepless nights.

This blog will explore how bed bugs infest homes in Melbourne, how they spread, and the early signs that can help you identify an infestation. Additionally, we’ll discuss why professional bed bug extermination is the most effective way to eliminate these pests.

How Bed Bugs Spread: The Truth Most Homeowners Don’t Know

The Silent Hitchhikers

Bed bugs are experts at travelling unnoticed. They hitch rides in travel luggage, on public transport, and in hotel rooms, spreading from one place to another with ease. 

These pests can also find their way into your home through second-hand furniture, clothing, and other personal items. Whether you’ve been on a recent holiday, stayed at an Airbnb, or simply used public transport, you may unknowingly be bringing bed bugs back with you.

Common Ways Bed Bugs Travel:

  • Travel Luggage: Bed bugs love to hide in suitcases, clothing, and shoes, allowing them to travel long distances without being noticed.

  • Public Transport & Hotels: Shared spaces such as buses, trains, and hotels are prime spots for bed bugs. They can hide in the upholstery or in the seams of furniture.

Why High-Density Living Makes It Worse

Melbourne’s growing number of apartment complexes and student housing developments provide the perfect environment for bed bugs to thrive. The shared walls, common areas, and frequent turnover of tenants make it easier for these pests to spread from one unit to another.

  • Apartments & Shared Walls: Bed bugs can easily travel through cracks and gaps in walls, from one apartment to the next, making high-rise buildings especially vulnerable.

  • Student Housing & Rental Properties: These spaces often have high turnover rates and can be more susceptible to infestations due to the frequent movement of residents and their belongings.

Common Myths About Bed Bug Spread

There are several misconceptions about how bed bugs spread and where they live. Here are a few common myths:

  • Hygiene Does Not Determine Infestation: Many people believe that bed bugs are attracted to dirty homes, but this isn’t true. Bed bugs will infest any space, regardless of cleanliness.

  • Bed Bugs Don’t Just Live in Beds: While people associate bed bugs with mattresses, they can hide in other areas of the home, such as couches, curtains, carpets, and even electrical outlets.

Early Signs of a Bed Bug Infestation in Melbourne Homes

Detecting a bed bug infestation early is key to stopping it before it becomes a bigger problem. Here are some common signs to watch for:

  • Bites & Skin Reactions: Bed bug bites are typically red, itchy welts that appear in a linear or clustered pattern on the skin. They are often found on exposed areas such as arms, legs, and neck.

  • Blood Spots: If you notice small blood stains on your sheets or pillowcases, it could indicate that bed bugs have been feeding on you during the night.

  • Shed Skins & Musty Odour: Bed bugs shed their skins as they grow, so finding small, translucent skins in and around your bed or furniture is a telltale sign. A musty, sweet odour often accompanies a significant infestation.

Where to Check for Bed Bugs:

  • Mattresses & Mattress Seams: Check the seams, edges, and underside of your mattress for signs of bed bugs or their eggs.

  • Couches & Furniture: Bed bugs often hide in the cracks and seams of sofas, chairs, and other furniture. Remove cushions and inspect carefully.

  • Baseboards & Wallpaper: Inspect around the edges of your room, including baseboards and behind peeling wallpaper, where bed bugs can hide.

Early detection is crucial because bed bugs can quickly multiply, making eradication more difficult and expensive.

Why DIY Bed Bug Control Fails in Most Melbourne Homes

While many homeowners attempt to control bed bugs on their own, DIY methods rarely offer long-term success. Here’s why:

  • Resistance to Store-Bought Sprays: Bed bugs have developed resistance to many of the insecticides available in stores. These sprays often fail to eliminate the pests, leading to reinfestation.

  • Hidden Nesting Spots: Bed bugs are skilled at hiding in cracks, crevices, and behind furniture. If these areas are missed, the infestation will continue to spread.

  • Spreading the Infestation: DIY treatments can sometimes make the problem worse. Inadequate treatment can cause bed bugs to move to other areas of the home, making it more difficult to fully eradicate them.

  • Delays Make Treatment More Expensive: The longer you wait to treat a bed bug infestation, the larger and more difficult it becomes to control. Bed bugs reproduce rapidly, so delaying treatment increases the cost and complexity of eradication.
Professional Bed Bug Treatment in Melbourne: How Experts Eliminate Them

Comprehensive Bed Bug Inspection

When it comes to bed bug treatment, a thorough inspection is essential. Professional pest control technicians use advanced tools like thermal imaging to detect infestations in hidden areas. 

This allows them to identify hotspots and assess the level of infestation. A complete inspection ensures that all areas of the home are treated, leaving no bed bugs behind.

Heat Treatment: The Most Effective Method

Heat treatment is one of the most effective ways to eliminate bed bugs. By raising the temperature in the affected areas, heat treatment kills both the adult bed bugs and their eggs.

  • How Heat Kills Bed Bugs & Eggs: Bed bugs cannot survive temperatures above 50°C, so heat treatment effectively eradicates them by raising the temperature in your home to lethal levels.

  • Why It Works Better Than Chemicals: Heat treatment reaches every corner of your home, including cracks and crevices where bed bugs may hide. Unlike chemical treatments, heat penetrates deeply into furniture, mattresses, and other areas, ensuring a thorough extermination.

  • Safe for Families & Pets: Heat treatment is a non-toxic method, making it safe for families with young children and pets.

Chemical Treatment for Severe Cases

For more severe infestations, professionals may use chemical treatments. These are stronger than over-the-counter insecticides and offer residual protection, preventing future infestations.

Why DIY Chemicals Don’t Compare: Over-the-counter chemical treatments often lack the potency required to eliminate bed bugs completely. Professional-grade insecticides are more effective and provide longer-lasting results.

Mattress, Furniture & Room-Level Treatment

Bed bugs don’t just live in beds. They can hide in sofas, cracks, and even curtains. Professional exterminators use a combination of vacuuming, steaming, and sealing to treat these areas.

  • Beyond the Bed: Bed bugs can hide in places like sofas, chairs, and even electrical outlets. Professionals treat these areas to ensure the infestation is completely eliminated.

Follow-Up Visits & Monitoring

A single treatment isn’t always enough. Bed bug professionals often schedule follow-up visits to ensure that the infestation has been fully eradicated. They will also monitor for any signs of reinfestation and provide ongoing support to ensure your home stays bed bug-free.

How Professionals Prevent Future Bed Bug Infestations

Once bed bugs are eliminated, professionals also take steps to prevent reinfestation:

  • Travel Precautions: Experts advise checking hotel rooms and luggage before bringing items back into your home. Always inspect your belongings after travelling.

  • Mattress Encasements: Professional pest control companies often recommend using bed bug-proof encasements for your mattress and pillows to prevent future infestations.

  • Regular Inspections: To ensure that your home remains bed bug-free, schedule regular inspections, especially if you live in high-density housing.

  • Avoiding Second-Hand Furniture: Be cautious when purchasing second-hand furniture, as it can harbour bed bugs.

Why Choose 7 States Pest Control for Bed Bug Treatment in Melbourne

7 States Pest Control is a trusted provider of bed bug treatment in Melbourne. With years of experience and a commitment to customer satisfaction, we are your go-to experts for effective bed bug extermination. Here’s why you should choose us:

  • Local Melbourne Experts: We understand the unique challenges of bed bug infestations in Melbourne’s homes and apartments.

  • Certified Technicians: Our team is fully certified and trained in the latest pest control techniques.

  • Advanced Heat & Chemical Treatment: We offer both heat and chemical treatments for comprehensive bed bug eradication.

  • Transparent Pricing & Guaranteed Results: We provide upfront pricing and guarantees, ensuring that you get the best value for your money.

Stopping Bed Bugs Before They Spread Further

Bed bugs are a growing problem in Melbourne, but with early detection and professional intervention, they can be eradicated before they spread further. Bedbugs control in Melbourne is crucial to prevent larger infestations that can lead to expensive treatments. 

If you suspect a bed bug infestation, don’t wait. Act quickly to avoid a larger, more expensive problem down the line.

If you think you may have a bed bug infestation, book an inspection or request same-day treatment today. Don’t let bed bugs take over your home.
